August 3, 2026

CareSource  
Attention: WI Member Appeals  
P.O. Box 1947  
Dayton, OH 45401

Re: Expedited appeal of prior authorization denial  
Member: Emerson Kimura  
Member ID: W623723443  
Plan: Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative  
Reference number: POC-0B7F2515DA-96515  
Requested service: Hip arthroscopy  
CPT: 29914  
Ordering surgeon: Reyes, MD

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria.

I ask that CareSource and Common Ground Healthcare Cooperative overturn the denial and authorize the requested procedure. The prior authorization packet documents a persistent, objectively confirmed condition and failure of appropriate nonoperative treatment:

- I have experienced 12 months of progressive hip pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I completed eight weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization, together with activity modification. The therapy period was April 30, 2026, through June 25, 2026, and included 16 completed visits. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment.
- I have used NSAIDs for eight months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on March 27, 2026, provided only two weeks of partial relief.
- MRI arthrogram on June 26, 2026, demonstrated an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement and an alpha angle of 68 degrees.
- The same imaging showed preserved joint space and Tonnis grade 0, supporting the absence of advanced degenerative joint disease.
- I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting and cannot run or squat.
- Examination demonstrated positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- There is no active infection or untreated substance use. BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

These records address the major medical-necessity issues relevant to this request: a documented structural abnormality, persistent symptoms, functional impairment, objective examination findings, failure of prolonged conservative management, and absence of the contraindicating conditions identified in the clinical record. The requested procedure is being recommended by Reyes, MD, an orthopedic surgeon, to treat the documented hip pathology.

The specific payer policy or clinical guideline used to deny CPT 29914 was not included in the denial notice and has not been provided to me. I have not quoted the plan’s medical-necessity policy because that policy text was not publicly retrievable or supplied with the denial. Please identify the exact policy or clinical criteria applied to this request, including its title, policy number, version or effective date, and the specific criteria that were found not to be satisfied. Please also provide the clinical rationale and records relied upon for the denial.

If any additional information is needed, please contact Reyes, MD, and allow the provider an opportunity to submit supplemental records or participate in peer-to-peer review. Please consider the enclosed clinical documentation, including the MRI arthrogram report, physical therapy discharge note, medication and injection history, examination findings, and the surgeon’s clinical assessment.

Please reverse the denial and approve hip arthroscopy, CPT 29914. If the denial is upheld, please provide a detailed written explanation identifying each unmet criterion and the evidence supporting that conclusion, along with information about any available external review.

Sincerely,

Emerson Kimura  
Member ID: W623723443  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Enclosures: Prior authorization denial notice; MRI arthrogram report dated June 26, 2026; physical therapy discharge note; treatment history; orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation
